This fictional article examines how big data analytics, machine learning, Bayesian learning, and accessibility ethics intersect in the development of transformative knowledge discovery systems. It argues that fairness alone is insufficient for evaluating intelligent systems used in disability-centered applications and proposes a broader justice-oriented framework for adaptive and cognitive algorithms. The paper blends perspectives from machine learning, Bayesian optimization, and critical accessibility studies to analyze risks in computer vision and decision-support pipelines while highlighting opportunities for robust, heterogeneous data modeling. result.title: Beyond Fairness in Transformative Knowledge Discovery: Bayesian Machine Learning for Accessible Big Data Analytics
